subject: jellyfish
pitch: A glowing moon jellyfish drifting upward. A translucent pale-blue bell with four pink horseshoe shapes inside, a frilly rim of fine tentacles, and four long, ruffled oral arms trailing below in pearly white and lilac. A soft glow lights it from within, like a lantern in the deep.
reasoning:
I'm thinking through the moon jellyfish model using the SDK, planning its real-world scale and positioning so the bell stays elevated with oral arms trailing below, respecting the pitch's instruction to keep it off the ground.

Since there's no transparency or emissive light support documented, I'll rely on pale, light-colored materials to suggest translucency and glow rather than true opacity. Now I'm figuring out the bell's geometry as a lathed shell, defining outer and inner profile points to form a dome wall with some thickness rather than a solid shape.

As an alternative, I'm considering just using a scaled sphere geometry with limited theta length to create an open dome shape instead of a lathe — simpler and more reliable, viewed as a thin shell open at the bottom, with flat faceting for a low-poly look.

Now I'm planning the gradient paint for the bell, lighter near the rim, and figuring out how to place four horseshoe-shaped pink gonad extrusions inside the dome at even azimuthal spacing, oriented so they're visible from above through the translucent bell like real moon jellies.

Working out the horseshoe outline geometry...

I'll set the bell joint position so the arm tips rest around y~0.8 off the ground, placing the bell center at [0, 1.3, 0], then work out where to position the horseshoe markings relative to the dome's underside given the sphere's scaled radius.

Since the dome is a solid, single-sided sphere, I'm weighing whether horseshoes should go on the inner surface (visible from below but hidden from above) versus the outer surface, trying to mimic the translucent look of real moon jelly gonads without actual transparency. I'll settle for placing them on the bell's inner underside at a modest height so they read clearly when viewed from beneath.

Actually I think I can make the bell read as translucent by lathing both an outer and inner wall, giving the dome real thickness and an inner surface visible from below. I'm working out the profile points for this double-walled lathe shape, defining the curve from base through the peak and back down the inner wall so it reads naturally from underneath.

For the rim, I want delicate frilled tentacles ringing the bell's edge — placing items in a circular pattern around the base, then for each one sweeping a short hanging bezier curve downward to suggest a dangling tentacle.

Then I move on to designing the oral arms: four longer, ruffled appendages hanging beneath the bell, following wavy catmull paths from near the rim down to tips lower on the body, with a frilled sweep profile to give them texture.

Naming each oral arm chain with sequential joints like "oral01" through "oral0N", parented to the bell joint, and giving the role "tentacle". I'm also planning to sweep ruffled frill geometry along the same chain path for the ribbon effect.

For color, I'll use a pearly white base fading to lilac at the tip via color bands, and consider a soft inner glow by placing a pale sphere at the bell's center or painting a gradient from bright center to cool rim since true emission isn't available.

For the horseshoe placements, I'm working out the rotation math so each horseshoe arc faces radially outward around the bell, computing direction vectors from the rotation angle and using their cross product for extrusion thickness, then positioning them at the correct radius and height.

I'm checking whether the horseshoe thickness could poke through the dome's wall at that radius, comparing the dome's outer surface height against the horseshoe's vertical offset to confirm it stays safely inside.

Then I work out the lathe setup for the bell, deciding the "at" point should sit at the bell joint position with the bone set to bell, and confirm the lathe function signature supports color as a Paint. I settle on making bell the root joint with the tentacle chain parented to it, without needing a separate hips joint.

For the glow core, I plan a small faceted sphere inside the dome using a soft white-pink color at the bell position. For the oral arms, I consider adding small ruffled details along the arm chain using torus shapes in lilac, oriented with their frame aligned along each point's direction, though I'm weighing whether this level of detail is worth the complexity versus simpler sphere-based "ruffle knobs."

I'm now thinking about using a ring arrangement around each arm point instead, with small spikes radiating outward in lilac to create a frill effect, orienting the spike direction using the frame's outward axis at each ring item.

Doing the math, this gives around 140 parts across all arms, which stays comfortably under the limit, and I'm tuning the tilt angle so the frill flares down and outward like ruffles rather than straight out. I'm also sketching out the color palette for the bell, rim, and glow core, and starting to work out the gradient paint for the bell surface.

Now I'm building the arm geometry: for each arm I compute a base point on the bell's underside and an outward direction vector, then generate five control points down the arm with a radius and height profile, adding a sideways sway using a tangential direction perpendicular to the outward vector. These points will feed into a Catmull-Rom curve to smoothly connect the arm's shape.

Setting up the joint naming for each chain, then defining the sweep function for each arm as a flat, tapering ribbon with a wavy ruffle effect along its edge using a sine-based radius modulation.

For the bell rim, I'm building a ring of tentacle-like sweeps using bezier curves offset outward from each ring frame item, checking that the ring radius sits just outside the dome base so the rim reads correctly.

I'm adding a small inner sphere as a glow core near the bell apex for a soft bioluminescent effect, then setting up the meta export and builder config for the moon jellyfish asset. Now I'm sketching a helper function to generate the horseshoe-shaped gonad outline by stepping through angles and plotting points around an arc.

Writing extrude call...

I'm working out the orientation vectors so the horseshoe opening faces inward toward the axis, then positioning it radially at a fixed distance with the bell joint as its anchor point, and planning to place four arms symmetrically around the center using the along function.

For each arm, I'm adding a ring of small lilac spikes tilted outward to create ruffled tips, relying on the frame data each chain item carries to orient the spikes correctly. Now I'm finalizing the color palette and writing the actual code for these rings and spikes.

For the arms, I'm setting up a tentacle chain built from a Catmull-Rom curve with named joints per span, swept with an elliptical radius profile. I'm also figuring out imports and drafting the bell's lathe profile points to give the dome a wide, flat moon-jelly shape.

I need to mark the axis points as sharp so the lathe doesn't round off the bell's center, and I'm settling on 24 lathe segments with some type-loosening around the outline tuples to avoid fighting TypeScript unnecessarily. I'll finalize the rim frill and tentacle sweep counts and skip adding extra glow spheres for now, then write out the complete code.
